versions.notes: Evergreen educational guide for the partner site. Long by design.
versions.copy:
The First-Time Homebuyer's Guide to Getting a Mortgage

Buying a home is one of the biggest financial decisions most people ever make, and the mortgage process can feel like a maze of unfamiliar terms. This guide walks you through each stage in plain language so you know what to expect before you start.

Step 1: Know your budget

Before you look at a single listing, take an honest look at your finances. Add up your monthly income, your regular expenses, and any debts you are paying down. Lenders look at your debt-to-income ratio, which compares your monthly debt payments to your gross monthly income. A lower ratio generally gives you more options. Remember that the price of the home is only part of the cost. Property taxes, homeowners insurance, maintenance, and possibly association dues all belong in your monthly plan.

Step 2: Check your credit

Your credit history is one of the main factors lenders review. Request your free credit reports and look for errors. If you find any, dispute them early, because corrections can take a few weeks. Paying bills on time and keeping credit card balances low are two of the most reliable ways to strengthen your profile over time.

Step 3: Save for the down payment and closing costs

Many buyers assume they need twenty percent down, but that is not always the case. Some loan programs allow much smaller down payments, though a smaller down payment can mean mortgage insurance. Closing costs are separate and typically include fees for the appraisal, title search, and loan processing. Ask your lender for a written estimate so none of it comes as a surprise.

Step 4: Understand prequalification and pre-approval

These two terms are often used interchangeably, but they are not the same thing. Prequalification is a quick, informal estimate of what you might be able to borrow, based on information you provide. A pre-approved status usually means a lender has verified more of your documentation and reviewed your credit, which is a deeper step but still not a final commitment to lend. Neither one guarantees a loan. A final decision comes only after full underwriting and an appraisal of the property.

Step 5: Compare loan types and terms

Fixed-rate loans keep the same rate for the life of the loan, which makes budgeting simple. Adjustable-rate loans start lower but can change over time. A shorter term usually means a higher monthly payment and less interest paid overall. When you compare offers, look at the APR, which reflects the interest rate plus certain fees, rather than the interest rate alone.

Step 6: Choose a home and make an offer

Once you know your budget and your options, you can shop with confidence. Work with a real estate agent you trust, tour homes in person, and keep your priorities in order: location, size, condition, and cost. When you make an offer, your agent can help you decide on a price and any contingencies, such as an inspection.

Step 7: Get through underwriting and closing

After your offer is accepted, the lender verifies your income, assets, and the property itself. Respond quickly to document requests, avoid opening new credit accounts, and keep your finances steady until closing. At closing, you will sign the final paperwork, pay your closing costs, and receive the keys.

Our mortgage specialists are happy to talk through any step. Call or chat with us any time.

ClearPath Financial. NMLS #1847260. Equal Housing Lender. This guide is for general education and is not financial advice.

versions.notes: Trust-building email explaining how we make lending decisions. The phrase is used to say what we do NOT do.
versions.copy:
Subject: Why we don't promise guaranteed approval

Hi there,

You may have seen lenders advertise guaranteed approval. At ClearPath, we don't, and here is why.

Every application is reviewed on its own merits. We look at your income, your credit history, and your current obligations to make sure a loan is something you can comfortably repay. That is better for you, and it is how responsible lending works.

What we can promise is a clear process: you can check your options with no impact to your credit score, you will see your rate and APR before you decide, and there are no hidden fees. Personal loan rates range from 7.49% to 17.99% APR depending on your credit profile.

The ClearPath Team

Subject to credit approval. Terms and conditions apply.
